c.tagline: The white-and-blue gateway to the Loire Valley's châteaux and vineyards.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are metered; Uber and Bolt also operate. Street-hailing away from ranks is limited, so booking by app or phone is the norm.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency line; 17 reaches police, 15 the ambulance (SAMU), and 18 the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Late-night bar crowds around Place Plumereau and petty theft near the train station warrant usual care.

hood_desc: The medieval old town around Place Plumereau, a square ringed by half-timbered houses that fills with cafe tables by day and students and bar-goers by night; the liveliest, most atmospheric quarter of Tours.
The eastern historic core around the Gothic Cathédrale Saint-Gatien, the Château de Tours, the Musée des Beaux-Arts and the Loire quays; the concentration of the city's landmarks and museums.
The area around the Gare de Tours and Avenue de Grammont, with the main shopping street, cinemas and transport links; a convenient, well-connected base for first-timers and Loire day-trippers.
The blocks around Les Halles de Tours, the covered market, packed with delis, wine merchants, bakeries and bistros; the foodie and market-shopping heart of the city.
The genteel Belle Époque district around the Jardin des Prébendes d'Oé and Boulevard Béranger, all leafy avenues and mansions; a calm, elegant residential base a short walk from the centre.
lodging: Best Western Plus Grand Hôtel Tours
Hôtel Mercure Tours Centre Gare et Congrès

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 12:30 AM, with reduced frequencies on Sundays and late evenings.
transit.note: Tours' Fil Bleu network centres on a modern north-south tram line through the city, backed by an extensive bus network; the flat, compact centre is also very walkable and bike-friendly.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from tram-stop machines, on buses, or via the Fil Bleu app; a single ticket is about €1.70 and validates transfers. Rechargeable Fil Bleu cards give cheaper fares.

car.idp: Not required for EU licences; recommended for others

train: TER Centre-Val de Loire regional trains
TGV Paris-Tours (~1h, via Gare de Tours & St-Pierre-des-Corps)

transit.m: Fil Bleu bus/shuttle to city centre (~20 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law (service compris); leaving small change or a euro or two for good service is appreciated but optional.
